analysis.title: McElligott: $47BN In Levered ETF Selling, $61BN In Vol Control As The "Best Trade Of The Year" Implodes
key_insights: Nomura estimates the levered ETF complex must sell $47.0B at the close, a 0th percentile reading and the 2nd largest in Nomura's data history behind $51.3B on June 5. 86% of the AUM is Tech Leadership / AI-centric. Morgan Stanley's estimate was $52B.
Breakdown of the projected levered ETF rebalance: Tech -20.5B, Mag7 -17.3B, Semis -4.2B, SPX -3.9B, all in the 0th percentile.
Clients are cutting risk after a 'Stocks Down' signal and capitulation headlines on hedge fund performance, citing preservation of remaining YTD performance into next year's fresh capital.
Pain is concentrated in legacy crowded trades: AI Momentum (long enablers vs short hyperscalers), Energy as a rates-short proxy and Iran hedge, and short-bond CTA positioning.
Nomura's crowding scoreboard: US Equities Momentum factor -11.9% in 5 days and -23.1% QTD, XLE -10.4% MTD, Crude Oil / Inflation Tail basket -13.6% in a week.
CTA trigger levels show a +2% bond move implies about $225B of global bond buying, led by $69.5B EUR 2Y, $48.5B USD 2Y and $23.9B JGB 10Y.

The Semis-Energy barbell, up 66% on a 3.3 Sharpe a few weeks ago, is down 13% in a week (Energy -10.2% WTD, Semis -13.1% WTD). The AI Enablers vs Hyperscalers pair is down 15% from its +80.4% peak on June 22.

Two drivers of the unwind: the election result, read as an anti-data-center/AI platform with positioning still stuffed in AI (Goldman sees moratoria freezing 45% of data center capacity), and a perceived White House shift toward easing on Iran that is removing the energy war premium. Brent is on track for its worst week since COVID.

VVIX rose 30 points to 122 after falling 17 the day before. The 1-day VVIX residual versus VIX sits in the 94th-96th percentile. VXN rose 12.96 points to 38.04 on a 5.88% NDX drop, a 99.8th percentile residual over 1 year.
Mag7 skew, ATM vol and put skew are near highs (89th, 85th, 88th percentile) while call skew is at the 11th percentile, so there is little demand for upside.
Mechanical flows: dealer negative gamma -$7B per 1%, vol control about $61B of selling implied (including about $25B from yesterday on lag), levered ETF -$47.0B. Total is over $100B of known supply.

Recent outlier-move days have tended to make the intraday low in the 2pm-3pm window before front-runners cover and the market closes off the lows. McElligott flags the risk that the bounce does not come and the market closes on its lows.

Vol control selling is $61.2B at the S&P's -3.76% move, rising to $70B on a -10% day. 1-month realized vol is 18.8, in the 94.8th percentile. UBS estimates $95-105B of risk control selling on a 2% SPX decline.

sector_views.rationale: Energy sector's war premium is being removed as the White House appears to be losing resolve on Iran. XLE is down 10.4% MTD and Brent is heading for its worst week since COVID.
Post-election AI liquidation, with positioning still crowded across hedge funds, mutual funds, retail and others, and levered ETF selling concentrated in tech and semis.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up 30 points on the day after falling 17 points the day before, a large outlier versus the VIX move.
Up 12.96 points on a 5.88% NDX decline, a 99.8th percentile residual over 1 year.
94.8th percentile, which keeps vol control funds selling into next week.

risk_factors: The usual late-day bounce does not arrive and the market closes on its lows as front-runners become the flow.
Over $100B of known mechanical supply (vol control, levered ETFs, dealer gamma) is concentrated at the close.
Short-bond CTA positioning could force further covering, with about $225B of buying on a +2% bond move.
AI positioning remains crowded across all investor types.
Data center moratoria after the election, which Goldman sizes at 45% of capacity.
vol_and_positioning: VVIX +30 to 122, a 94th-96th percentile outlier versus VIX across lookbacks, after a 17-point drop the day before.
VXN at 38.04, up 12.96 points on a 5.88% NDX drop.
Mag7 skew, ATM vol and put skew are at the 89th, 85th and 88th percentiles. Call skew is at the 11th percentile.
Dealer negative gamma is -$7B per 1%, with the peak at -4% versus -2%.
Vol control selling is about $61B implied, rising to $70B on a -10% day. UBS estimates $95-105B of risk control selling on a 2% SPX decline.
Hedge fund flows from the UBS desk ran 23/75/2 buy/sell/short sell.
Levered ETF rebalance of -$47.0B, with 86% of AUM in tech and AI-centric funds.
geopolitical: The White House appears to be losing resolve on Iran, which is removing the energy sector's war premium.
US midterm election result read as an anti-data-center / AI and anti-energy-industry platform.
cross_bank_references: Morgan Stanley's derivatives team calculated $52B in levered ETF selling at the close, versus Nomura's $47.0B.
UBS has a similar but larger read, with risk control rebalance estimates of $95-105B on a 2% SPX decline.
Goldman sees moratoria freezing 45% of data center capacity.
Goldman's derivatives desk noted VVIX fell 17 points and its Panic Index posted its second-largest one-day drop in 20 years.

tension_points.bear_case: The mechanical flows are so large (over $100B) that the usual bounce may not come, and the market could close on its lows after the front-runners' assumption fails.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No bounce from the 2pm-3pm window into the close, with the market making new lows into the standard TWAP.
